title: Automate chaos catalogue part 1 - exchange and transport faults
body:
## Context
With the harness from E45-T06 in place, this ticket automates the **exchange and transport half** of the chaos catalogue in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9 and the matching failure-register rows F1-F6 and F14 in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11. US-OBS-006 states the user-visible contract: *"Given the market WS is forcibly dropped in a test environment, then reconnection, resubscription, book resync and gap recording all behave as specified and are asserted automatically"* and *"Given the exchange returns 5xx and rate-limit errors, then backoff, user messaging and the dead man's switch behave as specified"*.

The most safety-critical scenario - private WS drop mid-order-lifecycle - has a step-by-step asserted sequence in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9.1, implemented as `test_private_ws_reconnect_reconciliation.py`.

## Scope / Deliverables
Automated scenarios, each combining the shared post-conditions from E45-T06 with scenario-specific assertions:
- **F1 / WS disconnect (public)** - drop mid-stream; assert detection within one missed-heartbeat interval, reconnect with backoff, resubscription batched at <=10 topics per request, fresh book snapshot, no stale data rendered as live, and a recorded coverage gap.
- **F1b / WS disconnect storm** - 10 consecutive drops within 60 s; assert backoff escalation (1/2/4/8 s capped at 30 s, jittered), no unbounded reconnect loop, and no duplicate subscriptions once the storm settles.
- **F3 / WS disconnect (private)** - drop mid-order-lifecycle; implement `test_private_ws_reconnect_reconciliation.py` to the section 9.1 sequence exactly: re-auth, `GET /v5/order/realtime` plus `GET /v5/position/list`, pair by the bound exchange order id, else by `order_link_id` and the full match (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.3 rules 3 and 7, as G-6 (#2876) set them), backfill executions for the gap window, re-verify the native SL invariant, persist, emit reconciled state. Assert "EXECUTION DEGRADED" is surfaced and rules are suspended while the private stream is down.
- **F2 / Sequence gap** - doctor a delta stream to skip a `seq`; assert the book goes `DESYNCED`, derived publication for that symbol stops, a fresh snapshot is forced, and no corrupt book reaches the OMS, the rule engine or the renderer.
- **F4 / Exchange 5xx on submit** - `500/502/503` on an order create; assert the create is never resent (its outcome is ambiguous: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.6, order creates, SR-E29-15), the order goes to `unknown` and reconciliation resolves it, adopting an order it finds only after the full match (section 8.3 rule 3), a distinct state is shown to the UI meanwhile, and the attempt is never silently dropped; a 5xx on an amend, cancel or `trading-stop` is retried with backoff (section 8.6).
- **F4b / Exchange 403** - assert it is treated as an auth/permission failure, not retried blindly, surfaced distinctly, and that the account is marked rather than spun on.
- **F4c / Rate-limit `10018` flood** - sustained rate-limit errors; assert `X-Bapi-Limit-Status`-driven backoff, that the `critical` bucket is never starved by `poll` traffic, and that fan-out degrades gracefully: accounts inside budget complete **with native SL intact**, deferred or failed accounts are reported per account, and no account executes without its stop.
- **F5 / Clock skew (`10002`)** - shift the clock past `recv_window`; assert `10002` is surfaced distinctly from a generic auth failure, order entry is blocked with an explicit actionable diagnostic, and the periodic `GET /v5/market/time` offset calculation recovers it.
- **F14 / Partial fan-out failure** - reject the order for one of N accounts in a trade group; assert successful legs stay live with native SL, the group is marked `PARTIAL`, per-account results are reported, and **no automatic retry** occurs that could breach a risk cap without explicit user action.

## Out of scope
- Infrastructure, host-clock, disk and client faults - **E45-T08**.
- The harness mechanism itself - E45-T06.
- The manual game-day pass and its sign-off - E45-Q02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Private-WS drop leaves no uncertainty
  Given an order is submitted and the private WS is dropped before its ack
  When the connection is restored and reconciliation completes
  Then the order resolves out of Unknown within two passes, no second exchange order exists for its order_link_id, every open position carries a native stop, and every execution in the gap window is present locally

Scenario: Sequence gap never yields a corrupt book
  Given a delta with a skipped seq is delivered for BTCUSDT
  Then the book for BTCUSDT transitions to DESYNCED, derived publication for that symbol stops, a fresh snapshot is requested, and no OMS or rule-engine read observed the gapped state

Scenario: Rate-limit flood degrades fan-out gracefully
  Given a five-account fan-out is submitted while the exchange returns 10018 for two accounts
  Then the three accounts inside budget are filled and each carries a native stop, the group is reported PARTIAL naming the two deferred accounts, and no order was placed without a stop

Scenario: Clock skew blocks the order path but not risk reduction
  Given the local clock is shifted beyond recv_window
  Then new order entry is blocked with an explicit clock-sync diagnostic, while cancel and close-position paths remain available

Scenario: Every scenario ends reconciled
  Given any scenario in this ticket completes
  Then oms_unknown_orders is 0, no order_link_id maps to two exchange orders, and the local and remote position sets are identical
```

## Technical notes / design
- Scenario ids mirror the architecture failure register (`F1`, `F1b`, `F2`, `F3`, `F4`, `F4b`, `F4c`, `F5`, `F14`).
- Bybit error codes exercised: `10002`, `10006`, `10018`, `110001`, `110079`, plus HTTP `403` and `5xx`.
- The private-WS scenario asserts the section 9.1 sequence **step by step**, not merely its end state, so an ordering regression (for example resuming the subscription before reconciliation) fails the test.
- Scenarios drive the real reconciler (E29-T06's pass and job, with E45-T01's carries and E45-T02's boot gate) and the real rate governor (E34) - no stubs on the code under test; only the exchange side is a fixture.
- "Fails closed on the order path, risk-reducing actions still work" is asserted as a pair in every fault scenario, per SR-154.

## Test plan
These tests are the deliverable. In addition: each scenario runs twice in CI (cold and warm cache) to catch state leakage, and each carries a recovery-budget assertion (<=5 s to usable after a 30 s outage; RTO <=90 s where a restart is involved). ## Security notes
SR-154 is satisfied in part here; SR-058 (reconcile on connect, reconnect and timer) and SR-083 (idempotent, retrying kill switch) are exercised. No production credentials are used; the mock exchange only.

UI-visible assertions (execution-degraded messaging, blocked order entry) check for *text* presence, matching the contract in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` that state is never colour-only. The full a11y audit is E45-Q03.

This half must run in <=10 minutes in CI. Backoff assertions use injected virtual time wherever possible rather than real sleeps, so the suite is not dominated by waiting.

title: Automate chaos catalogue part 2 - infrastructure, clock and client faults
body:
## Context
The second half of the catalogue covers faults **below and beside** the exchange: the datastores, the host and the desktop client. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9 requires "DB down (QuestDB or Postgres unavailable)" coverage; **SR-154** additionally requires DB unavailability and disk-full; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11 specifies expected behaviour for F7 (backend crash with open positions, RTO <=90 s), F8 (Postgres unavailable), F9 (QuestDB unavailable), F10 (disk full), F11 (slow WS client) and F15 (Electron GPU/renderer crash). The roadmap names "Postgres failover, QuestDB unavailability, disk-full, clock skew, Electron renderer crash mid-order" explicitly in E45's scope.

The through-line is identical to part 1: **fail closed on the order path, keep risk-reducing actions working, end reconciled**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **F8 / Postgres unavailable** - stop the container mid-flow; assert order entry is blocked (we never trade what we cannot durably record), market data keeps flowing, audit and journal writes buffer into the bounded on-disk WAL and replay on recovery with no loss and no duplication, and the health surface reflects DB-down immediately.
- **F8b / Postgres failover** - restart into a promoted instance; assert connection-pool recovery, that no in-flight transaction is half-applied, and that the first post-recovery action is a reconciliation pass.
- **F9 / QuestDB unavailable** - assert the recorder spills to the on-disk WAL, live views are unaffected, the WAL replays on recovery, and that beyond a 1 GB spill the lowest-priority symbols stop recording with an explicit coverage gap recorded rather than a silent hole.
- **F10 / Disk full** - fill the volume; assert auto-record pauses at 90 %, hard-stops at 95 % with an alert, the coverage gap is recorded, and trading is unaffected by recorder pressure.
- **F7 / Backend crash with open positions** - SIGKILL the backend with open positions and armed rules; assert positions remain protected by the native exchange SL, that on restart the order is self-check -> reconcile -> re-arm (rules must not evaluate before reconciliation completes), that emulated algos (TWAP, iceberg, chase) pause and are then resumed or cancelled per algo policy, and that **RTO <=90 s** to fully reconciled trading is met and recorded.
- **F5b / Host clock skew across a restart** - combine a clock shift with a restart; assert the reconciler's `gap_from` computation is not corrupted by the skew (offset-aware per US-MKT-009) and that no execution is missed or double-applied.
- **F11 / Slow WS client** - a deliberately stalled client; assert the connection is marked SLOW, conflation increases, and the socket is closed with code 1013 at 5 s without affecting other clients.
- **F15 / Electron renderer crash mid-order** - kill the renderer between submit and ack; assert the backend lifecycle is unaffected (the client is not authoritative), that on relaunch the client reconciles from server state rather than local memory, that no duplicate submission occurs, and that when WebGL2 is unavailable the engine enters `degraded-2d` rather than failing open.
- Every scenario contributes a row to the drill report and appears in the game-day checklist consumed by E45-Q02.

## Out of scope
- Exchange and transport faults - E45-T07.
- Backup scheduling and the restore *feature* - E42/E04; the **drills** are E45-T09/T10.
- Performance regression budgets - E46.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Postgres down blocks trading but not truth
  Given the Postgres container is stopped while a position is open
  When an order submission is attempted
  Then it is refused with a distinct "cannot durably record" error, market data continues to stream, and the health surface shows the database as down within 5 seconds

Scenario: Audit writes survive a database outage
  Given 50 audit events are generated while Postgres is unavailable
  When Postgres returns
  Then all 50 events are present exactly once and in order, and the WAL is emptied

Scenario: Backend crash meets the RTO and re-arms in the right order
  Given the backend is SIGKILLed with 3 open positions and 2 armed rules
  When it restarts
  Then every position is still protected by its native exchange stop, reconciliation completes before any rule evaluates, and the measured boot-to-reconciled time is under 90 seconds

Scenario: Disk pressure degrades recording, not trading
  Given the recording volume passes 90 percent
  Then auto-record pauses and an alert fires; at 95 percent recording hard-stops with a recorded coverage gap, while order entry and position display remain fully functional

Scenario: Renderer crash cannot duplicate an order
  Given the Electron renderer is killed after submit but before ack
  When the client relaunches
  Then it renders server-side order state, no second order exists for that order_link_id, and the order's terminal state matches the exchange
```

## Technical notes / design
- Container faults use the chaos docker-compose profile from E45-T06; disk-full fills a small bind-mounted volume rather than the real host disk.
- The Postgres WAL-buffer assertions target the bounded on-disk WAL of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11 F8; replay must be idempotent keyed by event id, which is the property test.
- The Electron scenario runs under Playwright's Electron driver (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` E2E layer), killing the renderer process through the main-process handle.
- RTO measurement: the harness timestamps process start and the completion of the last account's first reconciliation pass, asserts the delta and publishes `chaos_rto_seconds`.
- Clock handling uses the offset from `GET /v5/market/time` (US-MKT-009), never the raw host clock, when computing `gap_from`.

## Test plan
The scenarios are the deliverable. Supporting unit tests: WAL replay idempotency (property test); the disk-budget threshold arithmetic at exactly 90 % and 95 %; `gap_from` under a positive and a negative clock offset. Every scenario asserts a recovery budget, not merely eventual recovery. Fixtures reuse `packages/fixtures/bybit/` plus a seeded Postgres dump for the failover case.

## Security notes
SR-154's DB-unavailability and disk-full limbs are satisfied here. Threat: a disk-full condition used to suppress the audit log (repudiation) - the control is that audit writes buffer and replay exactly once, and that audit WAL space is reserved ahead of recorder space so recorder pressure can never starve audit; both are asserted. title: Automate the rollback rehearsal and make its report a release gate artefact
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3): *"Rollback rehearsal executed on staging: previous tag redeploys cleanly, migrations are backward-compatible, feature flags flip without redeploy."* `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` makes rollback a PRR checklist item. Today that is a manual, undocumented hope; this ticket makes it a scripted, timed, repeatable rehearsal whose report is a release artefact.

The rehearsal matters most for **migrations**: a rollback must leave Postgres readable by the previous application version, or the rollback is theatre.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `scripts/rehearse_rollback.sh` plus a Makefile target performing, against staging: deploy tag N -> seed representative state (accounts, orders, positions, journal entries, rules) -> deploy tag N-1 -> assert the app boots, authenticates, serves `GET /health/ready`, reads the seeded state, and can place and cancel a **demo** order -> redeploy tag N -> assert forward recovery.
- **Migration backward-compatibility check** - a linter over the migration directory asserting every migration between N-1 and N is additive or compatible, plus a live check that tag N-1's ORM models load against tag N's schema.
- **Feature-flag flip check** - assert every flag introduced between the tags can be toggled through `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` **without a redeploy**, and that any flag needing a restart declares "requires reload" per the SCR-145 contract.
- **Timed report** `artifacts/rollback-rehearsal/<date>.md`: per-phase durations, tags involved, migration verdicts, flag verdicts, overall PASS/FAIL; attached to the release ticket and referenced by the PRR.
- CI wiring: on demand and automatically on every release-candidate tag; a FAIL blocks the release gate.
- `docs/runbooks/rollback.md`: how to execute a real rollback, the decision criteria, who authorises, and what to do about data written by tag N that N-1 cannot read.

## Out of scope
- Restore-from-backup drills - **E45-T10**; rollback is about code and schema, restore is about data loss.
- The deployment mechanism itself - E03/E44.
- Production rollback execution - this is a staging rehearsal; the runbook covers production.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A clean rollback rehearsal passes and is timed
  Given staging runs release candidate tag N with seeded accounts, orders and positions
  When the rollback rehearsal script runs
  Then tag N-1 deploys and boots, serves /health/ready, reads all seeded state, places and cancels a demo order, tag N is redeployed successfully, and a timed report is written with an overall PASS

Scenario: A destructive migration fails the rehearsal
  Given a migration between N-1 and N drops a column still read by N-1
  When the rehearsal runs
  Then the migration compatibility check fails naming the column and the migration file, the report verdict is FAIL, and the release gate is blocked

Scenario: A flag requiring a redeploy is caught
  Given a feature flag introduced in tag N only takes effect after a process restart and is not marked "requires reload"
  Then the flag check fails naming the flag

Scenario: The rehearsal never touches live
  Given the target environment resolves to anything other than staging
  Then the script refuses to run and exits non-zero
```

## Technical notes / design
- Migration linter rules: forbid `DROP COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`, narrowing `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE`, and `NOT NULL` additions without a default, unless the migration file carries an explicit `-- two-phase: <ticket>` annotation naming the follow-up ticket that removes the compatibility shim.
- Seeded state uses the same factories as the integration suite, so it stays representative as the schema evolves.
- Phases timed: deploy N-1, boot, readiness, smoke, redeploy N, total. The report also names the longest single phase, which is what a real incident's clock is dominated by.
- The smoke order runs with E44's typed environment pinned to `demo`, so a misconfiguration is structurally prevented from touching live.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the migration linter against a fixture directory with one compliant migration, three violating ones (drop, narrow, not-null-without-default) and one annotated two-phase migration that must pass.
- **Integration**: a full rehearsal against an ephemeral staging-shaped compose stack in CI, plus a deliberately broken variant asserting FAIL is reported (the canary).
- **Manual**: one operator-executed rehearsal per release gate, signed off in the PRR.

## Security notes
The script holds staging deploy credentials, read from the CI secret store and never from the repository; its logs pass through the E04 redaction serialiser. A rollback must not silently revert a **security fix**: the report lists every commit between the tags labelled `security` and the operator must acknowledge them in the report. The E44 environment guard prevents live targeting.

title: Automate the Postgres and Parquet restore drills
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 7 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3): *"Restore drill executed: Postgres restored to a scratch environment and the app boots against it; one symbol's cold-tier history restored and queryable. Time-to-restore recorded."* `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11.2 sets **RPO <=5 min** for relational data (continuous archiving plus nightly base backup) and makes a **monthly restore drill** a checklist item in `07-release-and-prr.md`. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup; this ticket converts the claim into evidence.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `scripts/drill_restore_postgres.sh`: take the latest artefact from `GET /api/v1/admin/backups`, restore it plus the WAL archive into a **scratch** database, boot the application against it in read-only drill mode, and assert: schema version matches, row counts for `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `audit_log` and journal tables are within the RPO window of the source, the audit-log hash chain verifies end to end (`POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify` semantics), and `GET /health/ready` reports green.
- `scripts/drill_restore_parquet.sh`: restore one symbol's cold-tier Parquet partitions from the backup tree into a scratch location and assert the data is queryable through the DuckDB path - a replay-shaped query over a known window returns the expected bar count and checksum.
- **Measured RPO**: the drill computes actual data loss (newest committed transaction at source minus newest restored) and fails when it exceeds 5 minutes.
- **Time-to-restore recorded** per store in `artifacts/restore-drill/<date>.md`, with backup sizes, verification results and the overall verdict; this report is the R4 gate evidence.
- **Integrity gate**: the drill fails loudly when a backup's recorded verification status (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/verify`) is stale or failed, instead of restoring an unverified artefact.
- Scheduling: monthly on `main`, on demand, and once per release gate; results surfaced on SCR-146 as "last drill: <date>, <verdict>, restored in <duration>".
- `docs/runbooks/restore.md`: the real-incident procedure, the decision tree (restore versus reconcile-forward), and the explicit rule that after any restore the **first action is a full reconciliation** (E29-T06's startup pass or its on-demand route, #914) - Postgres is authoritative for OMS, but the exchange is authoritative for reality.

## Out of scope
- Backup creation, scheduling and the SCR-146 screen itself - E42/E04; this ticket adds only the drill and the "last drill" datum.
- QuestDB hot-tier restore beyond snapshot verification - market-recording RPO is best-effort per section 11.2, so the drill records the gap rather than promising a restore.
- Offsite or cross-region strategy - out of scope for a self-hosted single-host deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Postgres restore drill passes and records time-to-restore
  Given a verified nightly base backup and its WAL archive exist
  When the Postgres restore drill runs
  Then a scratch database is created from them, the application boots against it, the audit hash chain verifies, measured data loss is under 5 minutes, and time-to-restore is recorded in the drill report

Scenario: Parquet cold-tier restore is queryable
  Given the backup tree contains BTCUSDT cold-tier partitions for a known week
  When the Parquet restore drill runs
  Then the partitions are restored to a scratch location and a DuckDB query over that week returns the expected bar count and checksum

Scenario: An unverified backup is refused
  Given the latest backup's verification status is failed or older than its verification interval
  Then the drill refuses to restore it, reports FAIL with the reason, and names the last known-good artefact instead

Scenario: RPO breach fails the drill
  Given the restored state is 12 minutes behind the source
  Then the drill fails naming the measured RPO and the 5-minute budget

Scenario: Restore never targets a live datastore
  Given the drill is invoked with a target that is not a scratch namespace
  Then it refuses to run before touching anything
```

## Technical notes / design
- Postgres restore uses `pg_restore` of the nightly base backup plus WAL replay to a recovery target time; the scratch instance runs in the chaos compose profile with its own volume and is torn down afterwards.
- The application boots against the scratch database with order entry disabled (a read-only drill-mode flag), so restored OMS state can never emit a real exchange call.
- Parquet verification compares a content checksum of the restored partition set against the manifest recorded at backup time, then runs the replay query path (DuckDB) to prove the data is not merely present but usable.
- Scratch-namespace guard: the target database name must match `^drill_` and the Parquet target path must sit under `/scratch/`; otherwise the script refuses.
- The drill emits its verdict in the same report format as E45-T09, so the release gate reads one artefact family.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the RPO computation; the scratch-namespace guard (positive and negative); the manifest checksum comparator.
- **Integration**: a full drill against a seeded compose stack in CI, including a deliberately corrupted backup asserting FAIL and a stale-verification backup asserting refusal.
- **Manual**: one operator-run drill before the R4 gate, with time-to-restore recorded and signed off in the PRR.

## Security notes
Backups contain **envelope-encrypted API keys, the audit log and all financial state** - the highest-sensitivity artefacts in the system. Controls: the scratch environment is as access-restricted as production; the drill writes restored data nowhere outside the scratch namespace; restored key material must remain undecryptable during the drill (the master key is not supplied to the drill environment) and the drill asserts the application boots into a "keys unavailable" state rather than silently decrypting, proving key separation per ADR-0009. The drill is audited (`drill.executed`). Scratch volumes are destroyed at the end and the destruction is asserted.

## Accessibility notes
The "last drill" datum added to SCR-146 follows the existing table contract - text status, never colour alone; it ships as part of E45-S02's surfacing work. Otherwise N/A.

## Performance notes
Time-to-restore is recorded and reported per store; target <=30 minutes for Postgres at the expected volume (about 1.2 GB per SCR-143) and <=15 minutes for one symbol's cold tier. Exceeding the target does not fail the drill but is flagged as an operational risk with a named owner.

`restore_drill_result{store}`, `restore_drill_duration_seconds{store}`, `restore_drill_measured_rpo_seconds`; audit `drill.executed` `{kind:"restore", store, verdict, duration_s}`; a `system_events` row visible on SCR-144.

title: Write the resilience runbooks and record ADR-0016 on reconciliation authority
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 9 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3): *"On-call rotation, escalation path and all runbooks from `07-release-and-prr.md` section 5.2 exist and have been read through by the rotation."* E45 produces the resilience half of that set. Separately, this epic settles an architectural decision that is currently implicit across three documents and must be written down once: **who is authoritative when local state and the exchange disagree, and what the system may do about it automatically**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0016 - Reconciliation authority and automatic correction limits** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, deciding and justifying:
  - The exchange is authoritative for the *existence and terminal state* of orders and for position size; Postgres is authoritative for *intent* (`order_link_id`, trade-group membership, rule ownership).
  - Corrections the reconciler performs **automatically**: transitions out of `Unknown`, execution backfill, adoption of `untracked` exchange orders into a non-managed state, and native-SL repair on an unprotected open position (risk-reducing, therefore always permitted - including while the kill-switch is engaged).
  - Corrections requiring a **human**: position drift beyond the instrument's `qty_step` and anything that would *increase* exposure - the system never does that by itself. No action brings an adopted `untracked` order under management in v1: the pass adopts it automatically, audited as `order.adopted_untracked`, and it stays unmanaged (BQ-17).
  - The two-pass abandonment rule for `Unknown` (`UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`) and the demo-retention edge (`DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED`, ids older than 6 days on demo).
  - The dead-man's-switch position - additive only, opt-in, unavailable for `linear` - closing or re-dating open question **OQ-04** in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- **`docs/runbooks/reconciliation.md`** - how to read a discrepancy report, resolve an `untracked` order, resolve position drift, what "stale account" means and how the Owner clears it (E45-S01's Resolve stale account control, which calls E29-T06's resolve route; a good pass never clears it, BQ-4), and the escalation threshold (any unresolved discrepancy older than 15 minutes on a live account pages the on-call).
- **`docs/runbooks/disconnected-while-exposed.md`** - the F3/F7 incident: what protects you (the native SL), what to check first, when to use the local kill-switch, and why the exchange dead-man's-switch does not help on USDT perps.
- Cross-links from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11 and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9 to the new runbooks, and a `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` update for any failure mode the chaos suite discovered that is not already registered.
- A **read-through record**: every on-call rotation member acknowledges each resilience runbook on this ticket, since the R4 criterion is "have been read through", not "exist".

## Out of scope
- The chaos-harness authoring guide (E45-T06) and the rollback/restore runbooks (E45-T09/T10) - this ticket only cross-links them.
- On-call tooling and paging configuration - E04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ADR-0016 is merged and decisive
  Given the ADR is reviewed by the Architect and the backend lead
  Then it states the authority split, enumerates the automatic and the human-required corrections explicitly, and records the dead-man's-switch position with a re-check date

Scenario: A new on-call engineer can resolve a discrepancy unaided
  Given an untracked order and a position drift exist on the staging account
  When an engineer who did not build the feature follows docs/runbooks/reconciliation.md
  Then both are resolved correctly without asking the implementing team, and every gap they hit is filed as a follow-up

Scenario: The read-through is recorded
  Then every member of the on-call rotation has acknowledged each of the four resilience runbooks on this ticket before the R4 gate

Scenario: The risk register reflects the drills
  Given the chaos suite surfaced a failure mode absent from 32-risk-register.md
  Then a register entry with owner, likelihood, impact and mitigation is added before this ticket closes
```

## Technical notes / design
- ADR format follows `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md`; 0016 is the next free id after ADR-0015.

- Runbooks follow the `07-release-and-prr.md` section 5.2 template: symptom, blast radius, what is still safe, first five commands, decision tree, escalation, post-incident actions.

title: Serve the four discrepancy resolution routes that E45-S01 calls
body:
## Context
E45-S01's Discrepancies view gives the Owner one action per kind of divergence the reconciliation pass leaves (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §8.5): **Cancel at exchange** for an `untracked` order, **Accept exchange truth** for position drift, **Attach protective stop now** for a position with no native stop, and **Force resolve** for an order reconciliation holds `unknown`. No route serves them. The E29-T06 re-scope (#914, its ruling of record `issuecomment-6512631079`) left E29-T06 with two Owner routes only, `reconcileAccount` and `resolveReconciliation` (BQ-7), and made E45-T03 the reports table and its reads. The epic's re-planning list asked who owns the four (#5123's call (b)), and the orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-30: this Task serves them, contract first, and S01 consumes them.

What exists today: `cancelOrder` answers `409 conflict` for an `untracked` order ("reconciliation decides it"), and B1 consumes and audits a `CANCEL` there (`audit_command_refused_unowned`, INV-B1-l). S01's three audit actions, `oms.untracked_resolved`, `oms.drift_resolved` and `oms.sl_repaired_manual`, are in neither `24` §15.5 nor `AUDIT_ACTIONS`. `22` has none of the four operations. This Task invents no contract: what `22`, `24` and S01 leave open is listed under Technical notes as Q1 to Q8 for the orchestrator, and the PR's first commit puts what the rulings give into `22` and `24` (C-6.1).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract first, in the PR's first commit** (C-6.1): `22` gains the four operations beside `reconcileAccount` and `resolveReconciliation`, in their house style (Q1), and `24` §15.5 gains the audit actions. `packages/protocol` and the Python models are regenerated (`make gen`), never by hand. The server follows in the PR's later commits, once Q1 to Q8 are ruled.
- **Rules the four routes share** (BQ-7's, as E29-T06's two routes apply them):
  - Owner only (`admin:write`, `scope: none`), enforced server-side (C-12.4); a Manager or a Viewer gets `403`, an unauthenticated caller `401`, and the UI's state is never the control.
  - CSRF on the write (`CsrfToken`, SR-041) and `Idempotency-Key` required (`x-idempotency: required`): the same key and body replay the stored answer with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and act once; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`; a call still running under the key is `409 idempotency_in_flight`.
  - Refusals in `reconcileAccount`'s order, after admission and the idempotency lookup: `404` for an account that does not exist or that this process's environment does not serve (C-2.11), and for an order or a position that is not that account's; `503 oms_not_ready` with `Retry-After` while the OMS is not ready; then the route's own `409 conflict` when its target is no longer in the state the action resolves (Q1).
  - **Step-up:** Cancel at exchange takes one (S01). Whether Attach stop, Accept exchange truth and Force resolve do is Q6's, as is the class: a challenge before Attach stop meets `22`'s carve-out that attaching a missing native SL is never refused (C-2.6).
  - **Audit, write-ahead (C-2.9).** Each route writes its record before anything is sent or changed: `oms.untracked_resolved` (cancel), `oms.drift_resolved` (accept) and `oms.sl_repaired_manual` (attach stop), and force resolve's action once Q5 names it. Each names the Owner (actor, role, session, address), the account in `after_state` as `account_id`, the order or the position as its object, the value before and the change asked for, and the `challenge_id` of the step-up grant it spent. Its outcome follows, best effort: success, or failure with the venue's `ret_code` and never its message, as `position.leverage_changed` records its outcome (`24` §15.5). A record that cannot be written answers `503 audit_unavailable`, and nothing is sent or changed. The actions are added to `AUDIT_ACTIONS` (`services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py`, a C-10.2 path) with their test in this PR.
- **Cancel at exchange** (`untracked_order`): a protective path. It never consults the stale standing (BQ-5, C-2.6), and it never meets the arm token, the `trading.oms_enabled` flag, live trading enabled, the B18 kill switch or the order-entry gate (the C-2.6 carve-out under `22`'s `Forbidden`, as `cancelOrder`). The cancel rides the `critical` lane, inside C-12.7's reserve for stop placement, cancel and flatten. It never cancels a stop that an open position relies on (C-2.6, Q3). The row leaves `untracked` only when reconciliation finds the order cancelled (`RECON_FOUND_CANCELLED`, INV-B1-l's own exit), never on the route's answer alone (Q2).
- **Accept exchange truth** (`position_drift`): S01's AC. The local position takes the exchange's size, a `position_snapshots` row with reason `rest_reconcile` is written, and the next pass reports no drift for it (Q4). It is refused while the account is locked stale, as S01 shows it disabled; its venue read rides the `poll` lane, as the pass's reads do (§8.7, C-12.7).
- **Attach protective stop now** (`missing_native_sl`): a protective path. It never consults the stale standing (BQ-5, C-2.6). It sends `24` §8.5 step 5's repair (`attach_missing_sl`), which goes through E29-T04's recorded-stop writer on the `critical` lane and uses §8.8 rule 3's fallback (E32-T02) where no record is in force (BQ-9). It sends the stop the Owner confirms, which S01 pre-fills from the profile's SL offset (Q1, Q8). It only adds or tightens a stop and never clears or loosens one: a loosening stays `setPositionTpSl`'s Owner path with an `sl_loosen` step-up (§8.8 rule 5).
- **Force resolve** (`unresolved_unknown`): settles an order reconciliation holds `unknown`, from the venue's order history as §8.5 step 3b looks it up (Q5). It is refused while the account is locked stale, as S01 shows it disabled; its venue read rides the `poll` lane (§8.7, C-12.7).
- **The follow-up pass.** After Cancel's or Attach's venue answer, success or failure, the account's job is sent `SWEEP_DUE` with `trigger: manual`, as `reconcileAccount` sends it, so S01's row is re-evaluated by a pass (S01's AC "A resolution that fails at the exchange is honest about it"). On a stale account no pass runs until the Owner resolves the lock (BQ-4), so no follow-up is sent and the route's answer is the only confirmation until then; the standing never refuses the action itself.
- **Metric:** `oms_manual_resolutions_total{kind,action}` (S01's name), labelled by `kind` and `action` only and never by account. Both names are on the label allow-list (`.semgrep/cv-obs-metric-label-allowlist.yml`), with closed value sets and a `max_series` cap; the metric is declared in `20-architecture.md` §12.1 and `observability/metrics_catalogue.py`.
- **Mount:** wire the routes beside E29-T06's two (its PR2b's module and `oms_wiring.py`, or `app.py`), add the four RBAC matrix rows (`services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml`, `state: executed`: Owner allow, Manager and Viewer `403`, unauthenticated `401`) and record the step-up classes in the step-up registry (`api/step_up.py`) as Q6 rules them.
- **Tests**: unit, integration and contract per the Test plan, including the forbidden-role, unauthenticated, cross-account, replay, step-up, stale-account and audit-unavailable cases, and the native-SL assertion on the cancel and attach paths (C-2.6).

## Out of scope
- The UI is E45-S01: the Discrepancies view, its confirmations, its states and its client-side idempotency.
- The pass, the triggers, B19's job, the stale rule and its unlock (`reconcileAccount`, `resolveReconciliation`): E29-T06 (#914). The four named carries, SR-E29-06 (ii)'s attach-first cancel of a foreign stop included: E45-T01. The reports table and its reads: E45-T03.
- S01's other actions: Investigate (S01 opens `getOrderDiagnostics`, which exists), Acknowledge and leave (Q7) and Mark rejected (Q5), unless their questions rule them in.
- The `divergent` wait (its items `anomalies`, `unpaired`, `held`, `sl_restore_refused` and `sl_tighter`), which `resolveReconciliation` ends: API-only in v1, no E45 control (ruled 2026-10-31). B1's `held` rows (`OPERATOR_RESOLVED` to `rejected`, `oms.held_resolved`, `28` B1's version-1 note) are not one of S01's four kinds.
- A human adopt action: none exists in v1 (BQ-17); B1's `ADOPT` stays denied.
- A B1 or B19 chart change, a migration and a new bus topic: none is planned (Q2 and Q5 name where one would be needed).
- Bulk resolution across accounts (S01: excluded in v1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The Owner cancels an untracked order at the exchange
  Given account sub_001 holds an untracked order that the pass adopted and audited as order.adopted_untracked
  And the order is not a stop on an open position
  When the Owner sends Cancel at exchange for it with an Idempotency-Key and the step-up the route requires
  Then oms.untracked_resolved is written with the Owner, the account and the order before anything is sent
  And one cancel is sent on the critical lane for the order's bound exchange order id
  And the row leaves untracked only when reconciliation finds the order cancelled

Scenario: A cancel the venue refuses is reported, never assumed
  Given the Owner sends Cancel at exchange for an untracked order on a healthy account
  And Bybit answers 110001 order does not exist
  Then the route answers with the venue's ret_code and no venue message text, and the order stays untracked
  And the attempt's record carries outcome failure with that code
  And the account's job is sent SWEEP_DUE with trigger manual

Scenario: A stop that an open position relies on is never cancelled away
  Given an untracked order is a TP/SL order on an open position
  When the Owner sends Cancel at exchange for it
  Then the route refuses it, nothing is sent, and the position keeps its stop

Scenario: The Owner attaches a protective stop to a naked position
  Given the exchange reports a position on sub_001 with no stop
  When the Owner sends Attach stop with the stop S01 pre-filled from the profile's SL offset
  Then oms.sl_repaired_manual is written before anything is sent
  And the stop goes through the recorded-stop writer on the critical lane and is confirmed by a read-back of the position
  And a request that would loosen or clear a stop is refused, whoever sends it

Scenario: The Owner accepts the exchange's position
  Given local state says 0.5 BTC on sub_001 and Bybit reports 0.7 BTC
  When the Owner sends Accept exchange truth for that position
  Then oms.drift_resolved is written before the change
  And local state reads 0.7 BTC, a position snapshot with reason rest_reconcile is written, and the next pass reports no drift for that position

Scenario: The Owner force-resolves an unknown order
  Given reconciliation holds an order on sub_001 unknown
  When the Owner sends Force resolve for it
  Then the order is looked up in the venue's order history as step 3b looks it up
  And B1 is sent what the lookup finds, as the pass sends it, with the route's record written before anything changes

Scenario: On a stale account the protective actions run and the others are refused
  Given reconciliation for sub_001 is locked stale
  When the Owner sends Cancel at exchange or Attach stop for sub_001
  Then neither consults the stale standing, and each runs as it does on a healthy account
  When the Owner sends Accept exchange truth or Force resolve for sub_001
  Then each is refused with 409 conflict and changes nothing

Scenario: Only the Owner may resolve
  Given a Manager session, a Viewer session and an unauthenticated caller
  When each sends each of the four routes
  Then the answers are 403, 403 and 401, nothing is sent to the exchange, no state changes and no resolution record is written

Scenario: An exchange-touching action needs a fresh step-up
  Given an Owner session with no step-up grant for the route's class
  When the Owner sends Cancel at exchange
  Then the answer is 403 step_up_required with a challenge bound to that request, and nothing is sent

Scenario: An account or an object outside the route's reach is not found
  Given an account that this process's environment does not serve, or an order or a position of another account
  When the Owner names it in a route
  Then the answer is 404, nothing is sent, and the answer does not say whether the object exists elsewhere

Scenario: A repeated request acts once
  Given the Owner sent a route with an Idempotency-Key and it was answered
  When the same key and body are sent again within 24 hours
  Then the stored answer is replayed with Idempotency-Replayed true, and nothing is sent or changed again
  And the same key with another body answers 409 idempotency_key_reuse

Scenario: No record, no action
  Given the audit writer cannot take the route's record
  When the Owner sends any of the four routes
  Then the answer is 503 audit_unavailable, and nothing is sent or changed
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 3, as the orchestrator ruled: four routes over services that exist or that E29-T06 and E32-T02 bring (the OMS's audited cancel service and the `critical` lane, the recorded-stop writer and its fallback, step 3b's history lookup and step 4's position apply, and B19's job for the follow-up pass). There is no migration and no chart change, so the work is the routes, the contract commit, the audit registrations, the metric and the matrix rows. The neighbouring patterns are E29-T06's two routes (the refusal order, the idempotency record, the write-ahead audit, `503 audit_unavailable`), `cancelOrder` (the `critical` lane and the venue's answers) and `setPositionTpSl` (§8.8 rule 5's loosening check at the recorded-stop writer). The routes reach the OMS through its facade and narrow ports, never the exchange adapter. They consult the stale standing (`oms/reconcile_standing.py`) synchronously, before any interpreter is told (C-2.21), and only on Accept and Force resolve. A problem body carries a stable `code` and, for a venue refusal, the venue's `ret_code`, which S01 renders. S01's open rows for a stale account stay listed until the Owner resolves the lock: no pass runs before that (BQ-4). That was the delta review's nit n-d3 on #5123, left for the owner of these routes.

**Open questions, Q1 to Q8.** They are for the orchestrator; none is decided here. Each gives what `22`, `24` or S01 leave open and the build's reading. The PR's first commit carries the contract that the rulings give (C-6.1), and no server commit lands before they are ruled.
1. **Q1, the operations' shapes.** `22` has none of the four. The reading: four `POST`s beside `reconcileAccount` under `/admin/reconciliation/{accountId}/`. Each names its target by an id `22` already defines (`OrderId` for Cancel and Force resolve, `PositionId` for Accept and Attach) and takes `reconcileAccount`'s refusal order and `x-idempotency: required`. The refusals reuse `22`'s rules where they fit (`reconciliation_locked` while stale, `nothing_to_resolve` when the target has left the state the action resolves). For Attach stop's body, S01 pre-fills the profile's SL offset and lets the Owner edit it; the nearest shape in `22` is the `Offset` (`{unit, value}`) that `SetTpSlRequest.stop_loss` takes.
2. **Q2, the cancel's path.** `untracked` consumes and audits a `CANCEL` (INV-B1-l), and `cancelOrder` answers `409 conflict` for it. The reading: the route asks the venue to cancel the row's bound `exchange_order_id` through the OMS's audited cancel service on the `critical` lane, outside B1's command path, and the row leaves `untracked` only on reconciliation's `RECON_FOUND_CANCELLED`, so B1 does not change. A B1 arm for the cancel would be a chart version bump under the single-writer `machine_hashes.lock`, outside this estimate.
3. **Q3, a stop among the untracked.** An `untracked` row can be a TP/SL order on an open position, the OMS's own Partial-mode stop included (OM-T05 of `docs/security/threat-models/E29-oms.md`; §8.5's `foreign_stops`). The reading: the route refuses to cancel a TP/SL order while its position is open (C-2.6). SR-E29-06 (ii)'s attach-first cancel is E45-T01's carry, and whether this route uses it is for the ruling.
4. **Q4, Accept against step 4.** §8.5 step 4 applies the exchange's position on every pass (`oms.apply_position`; the report's `position_drift` lists "Step 4's corrections, each with both values"). S01's AC has the Owner's accept rewrite local state, and E45-T11's ADR lists drift beyond `qty_step` as a correction that needs a human. What does the route change that step 4 has not? Reading (a): step 4 stops applying drift beyond `qty_step` and leaves it to the Owner, a `24` change to E29-T06's pass. Reading (b): the route records the Owner's acceptance of a drift that step 4 applied, which closes it in S01's view; that is a write against E45-T03's report, and E45-T03 then joins `blocked_by`.
5. **Q5, Force resolve.** S01 offers "Force resolve from order history" and "Mark rejected" with `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`, and names no audit action for either. BQ-15 holds a live `unknown` row older than 24 h and never abandons it. B1 has no arm for a human `rejected`: `OPERATOR_RESOLVED` outside `held` is refused (INV-B1-m), so that would be a chart change. Does the route run one row's step-3b lookup and send B1 what it finds, as the pass does? Does Mark rejected exist? Which action records it?
6. **Q6, step-up.** S01 requires a step-up on every action that touches the exchange (Cancel, Attach), and the epic's Security notes say every resolution action. The reading: `accounts`, the no-grace class that `resolveReconciliation` spends, one code bound to the request. Two points are for the ruling. Do Accept and Force resolve take one? And may a challenge stand before Attach stop at all? `22`'s `Forbidden` says that attaching a missing native SL is never refused by a synchronous check (the C-2.6 carve-out).
7. **Q7, Acknowledge and leave.** S01 offers it for an `untracked` order ("remains visible, remains unmanaged"), and the ruling's four routes do not include it. Is it client-only, or a fifth route recorded as `oms.untracked_resolved`?
8. **Q8, Attach stop's offset.** S01 pre-fills the profile's SL offset and lets the Owner edit it. But `24` §8.5 step 5's `attach_missing_sl` has the recorded-stop writer derive the stop and its reason (§8.8 rules 3 and 5): the record in force, else the fallback at `profile.fallback_sl_offset`. An Owner-edited offset is not an input the writer takes. Does the route pass a caller's offset, which is a writer change, or send the derived stop, so that S01's "editable" becomes display only? Settle this before the contract commit.

## Test plan
Unit, each route with fakes (a principal resolver, the step-up gate, the OMS facade and its cancel service, the recorded-stop writer, the reconciliation job and its standing, an audit writer, a clock):
- `401`, `403` for a Manager and a Viewer, `404` for an account outside the environment and for another account's order or position, `409`, `503 oms_not_ready` and `503 audit_unavailable`;
- the step-up challenge on Cancel and Attach (Q6); the CSRF refusal; the idempotent replay, the key reused with another body and the call in flight;
- the record written before anything is sent, with its outcome after the venue's answer;
- the stale account: Cancel and Attach pass, and Accept and Force resolve are refused;
- the C-2.6 refusal of a stop's cancel (Q3), and Attach never loosening or clearing a stop;
- `SWEEP_DUE` sent after each venue answer of Cancel and Attach, and none on a stale account;
- the metric counting `kind` and `action`, with no account label.

Integration (`@pytest.mark.integration`; recorded, redacted fixtures only, no network, C-13.5): each route against the fixture-replay mock exchange, covering a cancel answered and one refused with `110001`, an attach confirmed by a read-back, and the follow-up pass. Contract: the provider test generated from `22`, and Schemathesis on the four paths; the RBAC matrix rows run `executed`; the audit vocabulary test holds the new actions in `AUDIT_ACTIONS` and in `24` §15.5; the step-up registry sweep passes as Q6 rules. Safety-critical (`AGENTS.md` §6 item 9): ≥95 % coverage with mutation testing on the touched OMS modules, and an explicit native-SL assertion on the cancel and attach paths (C-2.6). The PR names the chaos scenarios it touches (C-13.6); E45-T07 exercises them.

## Security notes
The E29 threat model (revision 29) gives this ticket SR-E29-12 (an `untracked` order is never managed; no adopt action, BQ-17) and SR-E29-17 (it registers `oms.untracked_resolved`, `oms.drift_resolved` and `oms.sl_repaired_manual` in `AUDIT_ACTIONS` before their first emitter).
STRIDE, for E45-X01's flow 2 (operator → resolution endpoints → exchange):
- **Elevation of privilege (RBAC):** Owner only (`admin:write`), decided server-side, deny by default (C-12.4). The Manager and Viewer `403`s are tests, never UI state (E45-X02 abuse case 3).
- **IDOR:** the account in the path must be one this environment serves (C-2.11), and the order or position must be that account's. Ownership is re-checked at the data layer, never trusted from the URL (C-12.4), and a miss is `404` that never says whether the object exists elsewhere.
- **Replay:** `Idempotency-Key` is required. The same key and body act once, a changed body under the key is `409 idempotency_key_reuse` (E45-X02 abuse case 4), and a no-grace step-up grant binds to the exact request's fingerprint, so a swapped request gets a new challenge (`POST /auth/step-up`).
- **Spoofing (step-up):** a fresh step-up on the actions that touch the exchange (S01; the class is Q6's), with the grant's `challenge_id` in the record.
- **Repudiation:** a write-ahead record per action, with the actor, role, account, object, before and after values and outcome (C-2.9); no record means no action (`503 audit_unavailable`).
- **Tampering:** no route strips a stop that an open position relies on, and Attach never loosens or clears one (C-2.6). An exchange-controlled `untracked` order is never brought under management (BQ-17).
- **Denial of service:** Cancel and Attach spend the `critical` reserve, and the reads of Accept and Force resolve ride `poll`, so a burst of resolutions cannot starve order entry or protection (C-12.7).
- **Information disclosure:** no key, signature, venue message or raw payload appears in an answer, a record or a log.

The `security` label records the OMS paths, `audit/` and the RBAC matrix (C-10.2 paths, CODEOWNED by `@CandleViewer/security`).

## Accessibility notes
None directly (backend). S01 renders the answers, and each problem body carries a stable `code` (and the venue's `ret_code` on a venue refusal), so S01 can state the effect and the error in text.

## Performance notes
Each route answers inside S01's 2 s server budget ("its server result within 2 s or an explicit pending state"). The cancel keeps `cancelOrder`'s bounds: the `critical` lane's 5 s token wait, inside its 9 s bound. Nothing is added to a hot path: the stale check reads the standing's plain flag, and a route sends B19 at most one event per request, never per tick (C-2.20).

## Observability
`oms_manual_resolutions_total{kind,action}` (S01's metric; no account label). The audit actions `oms.untracked_resolved`, `oms.drift_resolved`, `oms.sl_repaired_manual` and force resolve's action (Q5), each with its outcome. `http_requests_total` per route from the shared middleware (`403`, `404`, `409` and `503` are visible by status). Structured logs carry the `correlation_id`; the account appears in logs only, never a payload or a venue message.

## Definition of Done

title: Resolve untracked orders and position drift from the admin discrepancy view
body:
## Context
The roadmap scopes E45 to include *"a discrepancy report and a manual resolution UI"* (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.2). The reconciliation pass (E29-T06, #914) deliberately does not resolve two classes of divergence automatically, because resolving them could **increase exposure** - and the system never does that by itself (the rule ADR-0016 records, E45-T11):

1. **`untracked` orders** - orders that exist at Bybit with no local row. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` states: *"anything at the exchange without a local row becomes `untracked` and is surfaced to the owner"*, and `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` describes such an order as one that *"was placed outside CandleViewer and was adopted during reconciliation"*. The pass adopts them automatically, as `untracked`, audited as `order.adopted_untracked` with the venue identity, and no human adopt action exists in v1 (BQ-17, the resolution of D6). They are never rule-managed and never auto-cancelled.
2. **Position drift** - a local position size that differs from the exchange's by more than the instrument's `qty_step`.

US-POS-008 gives the user contract for continuous reconciliation; this story is the human half of it. Without it the owner has an alert with no action, which is the worst of both worlds - a system that knows something is wrong and offers nothing to do about it.

Design is delivered by **E45-D02** (hi-fi and handoff), itself built on the **E45-D01** wireframes, both signed off at least two sprints ahead per the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **Discrepancies** view reached from **SCR-143** (Admin: system health, route `/admin/health`) and linked from the reconciliation-divergence alert, listing every open discrepancy across accounts: kind (`untracked_order`, `position_drift`, `unresolved_unknown`, `missing_native_sl`), account, symbol, detected-at, age, the local value, the exchange value and the delta.
- **Per-kind resolution actions**, each explicit and each audited:
  - `untracked_order` -> **Cancel at exchange** or **Acknowledge and leave** (remains visible, remains unmanaged). There is no adopt action: the pass has already adopted the order, automatically and as `untracked`, and a human cannot bring it under management in v1 (BQ-17).
  - `position_drift` -> **Accept exchange truth** (rewrite local state from the exchange, the safe default), or **Investigate** (open the order/execution diagnostics for that symbol and account via `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`).
  - `missing_native_sl` -> **Attach protective stop now** (invokes the same risk-reducing repair the reconciler performs automatically) with the profile's SL offset pre-filled and editable.
  - `unresolved_unknown` -> **Force resolve** from order history, or **Mark rejected** with the `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE` reason.
- **Step-up authentication and confirmation** on every action that touches the exchange (cancel, attach stop): CMP-044 ConfirmDialog wrapped by CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, with the exact effect stated in words - for example *"Cancel order 1234 on account sub_001. This removes a live order at Bybit. This cannot be undone."*
- **Re-run reconciliation now** control invoking the on-demand trigger exposed by E29-T06 (`POST /admin/reconciliation/{accountId}`, Owner-only, idempotent), with a per-account result summary.
- **Resolve stale account** control, shown on a stale account only, invoking E29-T06's resolve route (`POST /admin/reconciliation/{accountId}/resolve`, `resolveReconciliation`; Owner-only, step-up class `accounts`, audited by E29-T06). It is how a stale account unlocks: B19 leaves `stale_lockout` on `OPERATOR_RESOLVED` alone, and a good pass never clears it (BQ-4). The confirmation states the effect in words - order entry for the account opens again - and takes the reason the route requires (`ReconciliationResolveRequest`: the Owner's own text, 3 to 280 characters, no secret, written to the `oms.reconcile` record), in CMP-040 FormField with CMP-007 TextInput. The view shows the `account_stale` refusal lifted only once the server confirms, never optimistically; other gates, such as the kill switch and the risk caps, keep their own refusals.
- States per `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty ("No discrepancies. Last reconciled 12 s ago."), loading, populated, resolving (optimistic row locked), error (action failed at the exchange - the row returns to unresolved with the exchange's error code shown verbatim), and **stale account** (reconciliation itself failing for >120 s, order entry disabled, the banner explaining what still protects the user).
- Components reused, none invented: CMP-049 Table, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-040 FormField and CMP-007 TextInput (the resolve reason), CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock (raw exchange payload for support), CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-012 Badge, CMP-076 ConnectionStatus.
- Frontend data access through the reconciliation endpoints: the report reads delivered by E45-T03, the four resolution routes of E45-T12 that the per-kind actions call, and the on-demand and resolve routes of E29-T06 (`reconcileAccount`, `resolveReconciliation`), plus live updates over the `system` WS channel.

## Out of scope
- The reconciliation pass and its automatic corrections, including the automatic adoption of an exchange-only order - E29-T06 (#914); the carries and the boot gate - E45-T01/T02.
- The report persistence and its reads - E45-T03; the four resolution routes - E45-T12; the on-demand and resolve routes and the five reconciliation metrics - E29-T06.
- Health-tile and incident-log surfacing - **E45-S02**.
- Bulk resolution across accounts - deliberately excluded for v1: each exchange-touching action is individually confirmed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An untracked order is shown as adopted, never managed
  Given the pass has adopted an order at Bybit that had no local row, as untracked, and audited it as order.adopted_untracked
  When the owner opens the Discrepancies view
  Then the order is listed with Cancel at exchange and Acknowledge and leave only, no action adopts it or brings it under management, and the view offers no rule or algo action on it

Scenario: Position drift is resolved to exchange truth
  Given local state says 0.5 BTC and Bybit reports 0.7 BTC
  When the owner chooses "Accept exchange truth"
  Then local state is rewritten to 0.7 BTC, a position snapshot with reason rest_reconcile is written, the action is audited, and the next reconciliation pass reports no drift for that position

Scenario: A resolution that fails at the exchange is honest about it
  Given the owner chooses "Cancel at exchange" for an untracked order
  And Bybit returns 110001 order does not exist
  Then the row is not removed optimistically, the error code and its meaning are shown verbatim, the discrepancy is re-evaluated by an immediate reconciliation pass, and the attempt is audited as failed

Scenario: Exchange-touching actions require step-up confirmation
  Given the owner clicks "Cancel at exchange"
  Then a confirmation dialog states the account, symbol, order id and the exact effect in words, and the action does not proceed until step-up authentication succeeds

Scenario: A stale account is visibly locked, with reassurance
  Given reconciliation for account sub_001 has failed for more than 120 seconds
  Then the view marks sub_001 stale, disables Re-run reconciliation now (reconcileAccount answers 409 reconciliation_locked while stale) and every per-kind action that is not protective, states that order entry for that account is disabled, and states that existing exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected
  And Cancel at exchange and Attach protective stop now stay available, because cancel and stop paths never consult the stale standing (C-2.6, BQ-5)
  And it offers the owner Resolve stale account on sub_001

Scenario: The owner resolves a stale account
  Given account sub_001 is stale
  When the owner chooses Resolve stale account, reads the stated effect, enters a reason and completes step-up authentication
  Then the resolve route is called once for sub_001 with that reason, and the account_stale refusal for sub_001 is shown lifted only after the server confirms the unlock

Scenario: Empty state is a positive statement
  Given there are no open discrepancies
  Then the view shows "No discrepancies" together with the timestamp of the last successful reconciliation per account, rather than a blank panel
```

## Technical notes / design
- The view is a route under the admin area (`/admin/health` -> Discrepancies), RBAC-gated to Owner; Manager sees the list read-only; Viewer has no access (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md`).
- Live updates arrive on the `system` WS channel; a resolved discrepancy disappears on the next server-pushed report rather than purely on local optimistic state - the reconciler is authoritative over the UI, as US-ALGO-* already states for OCO.
- Optimistic UI is allowed only for the row-lock spinner; the row's disappearance must be server-confirmed.
- Every action is idempotent on the client: a double-submit carries the same client action id and the backend deduplicates, so a double-click cannot cancel twice.
- Numbers are rendered with instrument precision (`qty_step`, `tick_size`) from the instruments cache, never with naive float formatting.

## Test plan
- **Unit (frontend, >=80 % coverage)**: the discrepancy row reducer per kind; action-availability logic per RBAC role and per stale state; precision formatting at `qty_step` boundaries; error mapping for `110001`, `110079`, `10018`, `10002`, and the resolve route's refusals (`409 nothing_to_resolve`, `503 oms_not_ready`, `503 audit_unavailable`) into the action-error state.
- **Component/Storybook**: a story per state (empty, loading, populated with each of the four kinds, resolving, action-error, stale account) with axe checks on each.
- **Integration**: against the mock backend, each resolution action asserts the correct endpoint, payload and audit event.
- **E2E (Playwright, added in E45-Q03)**: cancel an untracked order end to end against the fixture-replay mock exchange, and assert the audit log entry and the subsequent empty reconciliation report.
- **Chaos interaction**: after each E45-T07/T08 scenario, the view must render the resulting discrepancies correctly - asserted in the game-day checklist.

## Security notes
Threats (full STRIDE in E45-X01): **Elevation of privilege** - a Manager or Viewer must not be able to cancel an untracked order, attach a stop or resolve a stale account; enforced server-side, with the UI merely reflecting it, and asserted in tests. **Tampering** - adopted orders originate from exchange data, which is untrusted input: they are adopted into a non-managed state, never auto-bound to a rule, and every field is schema-validated (SR-040). **Repudiation** - every action writes an audit event with before and after values via CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger; missing audit emission fails the test. **Information disclosure** - raw exchange payloads shown in CopyableCodeBlock pass through the redaction serialiser, so no signature or key material is ever rendered. Data classification: financial, high. Requires Security-engineer review (E45-X02).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`): the list is a real table with row and column headers, extending the CMP-049 contract; discrepancy severity and stale status are conveyed as **text**, never colour alone; every resolution action is keyboard-operable and reachable in the tab order; confirmations use `role="alertdialog"` with focus trapped and focus returned to the triggering row on close; a row transitioning to resolved announces politely via `aria-live="polite"` without announcing every incoming reconciliation tick; numeric cells use CMP-020 NumericText so screen readers read values with units. Audited in E45-D03 and E45-Q03.

## Performance notes
The view renders 500 discrepancies without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame (the SCR-144 table budget); live updates coalesce at 1 Hz; a resolution action shows feedback within 100 ms and its server result within 2 s or an explicit pending state. The page must stay responsive while the system it reports on is degraded - each row resolves independently, and no row can block another (the SCR-143 rule).

## Observability
Frontend analytics: `reconcile.discrepancy_viewed`, `reconcile.resolution_attempted {kind, action}`, `reconcile.resolution_failed {kind, code}`. Backend audit (emitted by E45-T12's endpoints): `oms.untracked_resolved`, `oms.drift_resolved`, `oms.sl_repaired_manual`; the adoption is audited by the pass as `order.adopted_untracked` (E29-T06), not by this story. Metric `oms_manual_resolutions_total{kind,action}`.

title: Surface reconciliation status and drill outcomes on SCR-143 and SCR-144
body:
## Context
US-OBS-004 requires that *"reconciliation divergence"* raise an alert; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-143 (Admin: system health) already promises a tile per subsystem with *"a number with units plus a state word, never colour alone"*, and SCR-144 (Admin: incident / connectivity log) already promises a chronological record of *"WS disconnects, resubscriptions, sequence gaps, exchange 5xx, rate-limit hits (10018), engine restarts and recorder gaps"* - which is exactly what the chaos drills and the reconciler produce. The `/admin/health` example response in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already carries `{ name: oms, state: healthy, latency_ms: 1, detail: "0 unreconciled orders" }`, so the shape exists and this story fills it with real data.

This story is the *passive* surface; E45-S01 is the *active* one. Together they mean the owner can see the truth and act on it without reading logs.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-143 additions**:
  - A **Reconciliation** tile per account: last successful pass timestamp and age, pass duration p95, open discrepancy count by kind, and the state word (`healthy` / `degraded` / `stale`), with a sparkline (CMP-024) plus its table alternative.
  - A **Drills** tile: last chaos-suite verdict and date, last rollback rehearsal verdict and duration, last restore drill verdict, measured RPO and time-to-restore - sourced from the metrics published by E45-T08/T09/T10.
  - A link into the Discrepancies view (E45-S01) labelled with the open count.
  - `stale` accounts rendered prominently with the same reassurance wording used on SCR-152: exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected.
- **SCR-144 additions**: reconciliation divergences and drill executions appear as incident rows (subsystem `oms` / `ci`), each with duration, impact and what the system did automatically; drills are explicitly badged **DRILL** so a reader never confuses a rehearsal with an outage; a filter to include or exclude drills, defaulting to excluded.
- **SCR-146 addition**: a "last restore drill" row, showing date, verdict and time-to-restore per store (data from E45-T10).
- Live updates over the `system` WS channel; every tile resolves independently so a failing subsystem cannot block the page (the SCR-143 performance rule).
- Components reused: CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner, CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-012 Badge.

## Out of scope
- Resolution actions - **E45-S01**.
- The alert rules and routing themselves - E04; this story only displays their subject matter.
- Backups scheduling and the restore wizard - E42/E04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The reconciliation tile states facts, not colours
  Given reconciliation last succeeded 12 seconds ago for all accounts with no discrepancies
  Then the tile reads "Reconciliation - healthy - last pass 12 s ago - 0 discrepancies" as text, and the same information is available to a screen reader without relying on the tile colour

Scenario: A stale account is unmissable and reassuring
  Given account sub_001 has been stale for 3 minutes
  Then the tile shows "sub_001 stale - order entry disabled - last good 3 min ago", states that exchange-side stops are unaffected, and links to the Discrepancies view

Scenario: Drills appear in the incident log, clearly marked
  Given the nightly chaos suite ran and one scenario failed
  Then an incident row appears for the run, badged DRILL, naming the failed scenario and linking to the archived report, and it is hidden by default under the "exclude drills" filter

Scenario: Health page survives the thing it is reporting on
  Given the OMS subsystem is unreachable
  Then the reconciliation tile shows "unknown - no data since <timestamp>" while every other tile continues to update normally

Scenario: Drill tile reflects the latest drill outcomes
  Given the restore drill last ran yesterday with verdict PASS, measured RPO 90 seconds and time-to-restore 18 minutes
  Then the Drills tile shows those three values with units and the run date
```

## Technical notes / design
- Tile data comes from `GET /api/v1/admin/health` (extended with a `reconciliation` block by E45-T03) plus `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents` for the log; drill outcomes come from the same health payload, populated from the drill metrics.
- Each tile subscribes to `system` at 1 Hz per the SCR-143 budget; no tile may await another's data.
- "Age" values are rendered from the server timestamp plus the known clock offset (US-MKT-009), never from a naive client clock, so a skewed client does not display a false freshness.
- DRILL badging is derived from the `system_events` row's origin field written by E45-T08/T09/T10 - not from string-matching a message.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=80 %)**: tile state derivation (healthy/degraded/stale/unknown) from the health payload including the missing-data branch; age formatting with a clock offset; the drill filter predicate.
- **Component/Storybook**: a story per tile state including "unknown - no data", axe-checked.
- **Integration**: mocked health payloads driving each state; a mocked `system` frame transitioning an account to stale and back.
- **E2E (E45-Q03)**: run one chaos scenario in the harness, then assert the resulting incident row and tile state in the UI - proving the wiring end to end rather than in mocks.

## Security notes
The health and incident surfaces are admin-only, RBAC-gated (Owner and Manager read; Viewer no access). Threat - **information disclosure**: incident details and drill reports can contain account identifiers and error payloads; they pass through the redaction serialiser and expose no key material, signatures or session tokens, and links to archived drill reports are authenticated rather than public URLs. Threat - **denial of service by observation**: the page polls and subscribes at bounded rates so a degraded backend is not further loaded by its own health page.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA: each subsystem is a labelled row or tile with a **text** status, per the existing SCR-143 a11y contract - no reliance on a dot colour; every sparkline has a table alternative; the incident table has real headers with severity as text, and long messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently (the existing SCR-144 contract); stale and degraded transitions announce once via `role="status"` rather than on every tick. Audited in E45-D03.

## Performance notes
SCR-143 must stay under 2 ms scripting per frame and must remain responsive while the system it reports on is degraded; SCR-144 must scroll 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame (both budgets are the screens' existing contracts in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`). Live incident rows append without a full re-render.

## Observability
Frontend analytics `health.reconciliation_tile_viewed`, `incident.log_viewed`, `incident.drill_filter_toggled`; the existing audited events `health.diagnostics_exported` and `incident.acknowledged` remain unchanged.

title: Wireframe the reconciliation, discrepancy and drill surfaces
body:
## Context
E45 introduces a genuinely new interaction that exists nowhere else in the product: **the system telling the owner that its own record of reality is wrong, and offering a small set of dangerous corrections**. Every other admin surface reports; this one asks for a decision with money attached. The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1) requires these designs Done at least two sprints before the consuming stories E45-S01 and E45-S02, which sit in Sprint 22 - hence Sprint 20 here.

The surfaces extend screens that already exist and already have design sign-off checklists: **SCR-143** (Admin: system health), **SCR-144** (Admin: incident / connectivity log) and **SCR-146** (Admin: backups & restore). The framing language is already established by **SCR-152**, whose reassurance line - *"Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected"* - is the tone this epic must inherit: state the problem, state what is still safe, offer the action.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Light UX research** (this is the `ux-research` label): a 45-minute session with the Owner walking through three recorded incident transcripts from the chaos drills, to learn what they actually want to know first when the system says "we disagree with Bybit". Output: a one-page findings note with the decided information hierarchy, filed in the Figma file and summarised on this ticket.
- **Wireframes** (Figma, low fidelity, greyscale) for:
  1. The **Discrepancies view** - list, the four discrepancy kinds (`untracked_order`, `position_drift`, `unresolved_unknown`, `missing_native_sl`), the local-versus-exchange comparison layout, and the per-kind action sets (E45-S01's; an `untracked_order` row has none that adopts it, BQ-17).
  2. The **resolution confirmation** pattern for exchange-touching actions - wording, what the dialog must restate (account, symbol, order id, exact effect, irreversibility), and where step-up authentication appears.
  3. The **Reconciliation tile** and the **Drills tile** on SCR-143, in all four states: healthy, degraded, stale, unknown/no-data.
  4. The **SCR-144 drill rows** including the DRILL badge and the include/exclude-drills filter.
  5. The **SCR-146 "last restore drill"** row.
  6. All empty, loading, error and edge-density states: 0 discrepancies, 1, and 500 across six accounts.
- **Content design**: the exact strings for every state and every confirmation, written with the SCR-152 tone - plain, non-alarmist, and always naming what still protects the user. Strings reviewed with the backend lead so no message promises behaviour the system does not have.
- An **interaction decision record** on this ticket for the two questions the wireframes must settle: (a) is resolution per-row only, or is bulk allowed - the recommendation is per-row only for v1, since each action touches the exchange; (b) does a resolved row disappear immediately or on server confirmation - the recommendation is server confirmation, because the reconciler is authoritative over the UI.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fidelity visuals, tokens, motion and handoff - **E45-D02**.
- Design QA of the built result - **E45-D03**.
- New design-system components - none are expected; if the wireframes require one, this ticket files a design-system contribution ticket against E05 rather than inventing a local one-off.
- Any mobile or Android layout - out of scope per the owner decision of 2026-09-14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

Scenario: Confirmations state the exact effect
  Given the confirmation wireframe for "Cancel at exchange"
  Then it names the account, symbol and order id, states in one sentence what will happen at Bybit, states that it cannot be undone, and shows where step-up authentication occurs

Scenario: Components come from the catalogue
  Given the wireframes are reviewed against 15-component-catalogue.md
  Then every element maps to an existing CMP id, or a design-system contribution ticket exists for anything new

Scenario: Research findings are recorded and applied
  Then the findings note exists, and the chosen information hierarchy in the wireframes is traceable to a specific finding rather than to designer preference

Scenario: Sign-off
  Then the Chief Design Officer and the backend lead have both approved, and the SCR-143, SCR-144 and SCR-146 design sign-off checklists in 14-screens-catalogue.md have no unaddressed item for the new content
```

- Information hierarchy starting point, to be confirmed by research: (1) is my money safe right now, (2) what disagrees, (3) by how much, (4) what can I do, (5) what happened.
